summary: Melia of Thebes is a Boeotian ash-tree nymph in Greek mythology, attested by Pausanias as daughter of Ocean, sister of Caanthus, lover of Apollo, and mother of Tenerus and Ismenus at the Ismenian spring. She is distinct from Melia the Argive Oceanid and from the collective Hesiodic Meliae.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: Pausanias tells how Caanthus, son of Ocean and brother of Melia, sought his abducted sister, found her with Apollo, and burned the god's precinct; Apollo killed him, and his tomb stands by the Ismenian fountain (Description of Greece 9.10.5).
By Apollo, Melia bore Tenerus, to whom the god gave divination, and Ismenus, eponym of the Theban river (9.10.6).
